requirements.requirement: Create a dedicated inventorysvc account on node1
requirements.summary: useradd --system --no-create-home --shell /usr/sbin/nologin inventorysvc succeeded and id confirms uid=996(inventorysvc), a proper dedicated system account with no login shell.

requirements.requirement: Run /usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker as a managed service named inventory-worker
requirements.summary: A systemd unit /etc/systemd/system/inventory-worker.service was created with ExecStart pointing at the target binary, then enabled and started; systemctl status shows it loaded, enabled, and active (running).

requirements.requirement: The service must run under the dedicated inventorysvc account, not root
requirements.summary: The unit specifies User=inventorysvc/Group=inventorysvc, and ps output directly confirms both the worker process and its sleep child are owned by inventorysvc rather than root.
Platform snapshots and command targeting confirm all actions occurred on node1 (RHEL 9.8, address 10.100.207.10) matching the managed topology.

requirements.requirement: Independent provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: pre-restart baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered service/data/cluster state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (377b5195...) and healthy enabled/active service state were captured, systemctl reboot was issued and acknowledged, the node became unreachable during two poll attempts, post-restart boot_id (5531ef94...) differs confirming a real reboot, and post-restart checks show inventory-worker active, enabled, and running as inventorysvc (new PID 716) - a complete before/disruption/after transition, cross-checked by the fixed after-prepare and after-executor boot-identity snapshots.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task were satisfied: node1 now runs /usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker as the systemd service inventory-worker under the dedicated, unprivileged inventorysvc system account, directly confirmed via ps and systemctl status. The independently required provider-wide restart evidence protocol was also fully and coherently demonstrated, with matching boot-identity baseline, disruption, and recovery evidence, and the service auto-recovered correctly under the same unprivileged account after reboot.
limitations: Evidence relies on a single executor attempt with no retries needed; captured outputs are trusted as presented and not independently re-verified.
No evidence of SELinux or firewall context specific to the worker was captured, though the task did not require it and the binary is a trivial sleep-loop script.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewing the full command timeline, every state-changing action ties directly to a material outcome or the mandated restart protocol: binary/user inspection (read-only), useradd (required account), systemd unit write + daemon-reload/enable/start (required service), boot_id/status capture (baseline), systemctl reboot (mandated restart), reconnection polling (read-only, two timeouts are expected transient failures during reboot, not state mutations), and post-restart verification (read-only). No unnecessary or unexplained mutations were found. The only residue is /tmp/reboot.log, a trivial byproduct of redirecting the backgrounded reboot command's output; it is tiny, harmless, and consistent with output capture for the restart step rather than abandoned troubleshooting. Failed-services and package-health checks remain clean pre- and post-executor.
